target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure (D113) defines trading cash instruments components (corporate debt, other debt, equity) and table presentation. The 2024 disclosures split this: D103 covers the table presentation (assets/liabilities positive/negative), and D105 covers the component definitions. These are distinct aspects of the same topic ('Trading Cash Instruments' table/notes) but presented as separate disclosures in 2024. They share the same SEC Item (Item 8) and specific subject matter (Fair Value Hierarchy for Trading Cash Instruments). They are kept as one grouped row to represent the many-to-many split from the single 2023 topic.

materiality_analysis.reason: Removal of the disclosure presenting trading cash instruments by fair value hierarchy level. Trading cash instruments are a core component of Goldman Sachs' assets and liabilities. Removing this specific tabular data (or its summary disclosure) significantly reduces transparency into the liquidity and valuation risk profile of the firm's most liquid trading assets and liabilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value hierarchy classification for exchange-traded derivatives
comparisons.peer_summary: Exchange-traded derivatives measured using quoted prices in active markets are classified as Level 1 within the fair value hierarchy.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Citigroup (C) disclose the classification of specific financial instruments within the fair value hierarchy levels. GS presents a table for 'trading cash instruments' showing assets and liabilities by level, explicitly stating that assets are positive and liabilities are negative. Similarly, C classifies 'exchange-traded derivatives' as Level 1 based on quoted prices in active markets. While GS focuses on the presentation of a broad category of cash instruments with sign conventions for assets/liabilities, C specifies the valuation input basis (quoted prices) for a specific derivative type to assign it to Level 1.

sentences.text: The table below presents trading cash instruments by level within the fair value hierarchy.
• Assets are shown as positive amounts and liabilities are shown as negative amounts.
Exchange-traded derivatives, measured at fair value using quoted (i.e., exchange) prices in active markets, where available, are classified as Level 1 within the fair value hierarchy.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value hierarchy classification of financial assets and liabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: A table presents the carrying values and estimated fair values at December 31, 2024 and 2023, for financial assets and liabilities excluding those carried at fair value on a recurring basis, classified within the fair value hierarchy.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) present tables that organize financial instruments by fair value hierarchy classification. GS's table specifically addresses 'trading cash instruments' and defines the sign convention (assets positive, liabilities negative) for the presentation. JPM's table presents 'carrying values and estimated fair values' for financial assets and liabilities (excluding those carried at fair value on a recurring basis) and classifies them within the fair value hierarchy. Both disclosures serve to map specific asset/liability categories to the hierarchy levels, though GS focuses on trading cash instruments while JPM includes non-recurring fair value instruments.
